title: PaCELab Equip: Shared Laboratory Equipment System
summary: A PHP web application on PostgreSQL (or SQLite) that records equipment use in a shared laboratory, charges each use to a grant account, prevents scheduling conflicts, and produces the monthly charge report for the business office.
requirements: Windows 10 or 11 for the drive copy; the bundled PHP in tools\php and the estate's PostgreSQL on the drive run it, so nothing is installed on the computer and no PHP on the computer is used
Start it from a normal window, never with Run as administrator: PostgreSQL refuses to run under an administrator account
On a campus server: PHP 8.0 or later with pdo_pgsql (or pdo_sqlite) and a folder the web server can write to
install: Plug in the drive and open the application folder under apps\pacelab-equip.

Double-click SETUP.bat. It creates config.local.json, points the data folder at ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\data, then runs tools\setup-machine.ps1, which checks the bundled PHP and starts the server. It writes nothing on the computer.
Double-click PaCELab Equip.exe, or open http://127.0.0.1:8147/ in a browser.

To start it at logon, run this once in PowerShell on each computer; it makes the shortcut Shared Lab Equipment in your Startup folder, replacing any older one, with its target through the estate's fixed folder: $s = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell; $l = $s.CreateShortcut((Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Startup')) 'Shared Lab Equipment.lnk')); $l.TargetPath = "$env:SystemDrive\Estate\App_to_Migrate\apps\pacelab-equip\PaCELab Equip.exe"; $l.WorkingDirectory = "$env:SystemDrive\Estate\App_to_Migrate\apps\pacelab-equip"; $l.Arguments = ''; $l.Save()
run: Double-click PaCELab Equip.exe in the application folder, or the Shared Lab Equipment shortcut on the Desktop. Either starts PostgreSQL on the drive and the server when they are down and opens the browser; a problem appears in a message box.
Double-click Stop PaCELab Equip.exe to stop this application's server and nothing else, then PostgreSQL on the drive unless another application still uses it. Do this before unplugging the drive.

Every other action is one PowerShell command in the application folder, written powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File followed by: tools\serve.ps1 status (is it running), tools\run-tests.ps1 (the regression suite against a scratch database), tools\backup.ps1 -Now (a backup now, proved by a restore), tools\reset-admin-password.ps1 (an administrator is locked out), tools\build-release.ps1 -Open (the zip for the campus server).

settings.meaning: The folder holding the installer lock, the logs and lab.sqlite, relative to the application folder: ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\data on the drive. Empty means data\ inside the application folder.
Where the daily backups go, relative to the application folder: ..\..\data\pacelab-equip\backups on the drive.
pgsql on the drive: the pacelab database on the estate's PostgreSQL, 127.0.0.1 port 5433, with its settings in pg.env beside the data folder. sqlite, or empty, means lab.sqlite in the data folder.
On a server, in the environment (env.template.txt lists them): pgsql and the PostgreSQL connection. Unset means the value in config.local.json, then SQLite.

data: The data lives outside the application folder: the pacelab database on the estate's PostgreSQL on the drive, and data\pacelab-equip\data for the installer lock and the logs, named by config.local.json. Neither is ever stored in git. Without config.local.json the application uses SQLite in data\ in its own folder, as it always did.
backups: While the server runs, it takes one backup a day (pg_dump on PostgreSQL, VACUUM INTO on SQLite), restores or reads it back and counts its rows before keeping it, and keeps 60 days in data\pacelab-equip\backups. tools\backup.ps1 -Now takes one on demand and proves it restores.
